No spam - genuine quotes from vetted UK engine specialists only. 8,000+ Engine Codes 40+ Car Brands 100% Free · No Obligation Make Select Make Series Model Select a model Year Select Model First Engine Code Get Free Engine Quotes At a glance · what your rough idle means Match the symptom pattern to the likely cause and urgency Rough idle, improves when driving Likely cause: Spark plugs/coils Low-Medium £60-£220 Rough idle + EML Likely cause: Sensor/actuator failure Medium £100-£600 Rough idle + black smoke Likely cause: Over-fuelling Medium £100-£900 Rough idle + misfire codes Likely cause: Ignition/injector issue Medium £80-£900 Rough idle worse when warm Likely cause: Valve/compression issue Medium-High £500-£2,000+ What this usually means in UK cars Four primary causes of rough idle A rough idle is one of the most common engine complaints - and one of the easiest to diagnose with the right approach. In our 24,650 quote dataset, we identified four primary causes: Ignition system (35% of cases) → Spark plugs, coils, leads. Repair: £60-£220. Vacuum leaks (25% of cases) → Hoses, gaskets, intake manifold. Repair: £100-£400. Fuel system (20% of cases) → Injectors, fuel pressure. Repair: £100-£900. Compression issues (15% of cases) → Valves, piston rings. Repair: £500-£2,000+. Sensor failure (5% of cases) → MAF, oxygen sensors. Repair: £100-£300. The key pattern: If the idle improves when you drive, it's typically ignition or vacuum. If it gets worse when warm, suspect compression or valve issues. Common affected vehicles & engines Typical rough idle issues by vehicle and engine code Vehicle Common Engine Code Typical Rough Idle Issue Cost Range VW Golf/Audi A3 EA888 2.0 TSI Coil pack failure £80-£200 BMW 3-Series (E90) N43/N53 2.0 Injector failure (direct injection) £300-£900 Ford Focus 1.0/1.6 EcoBoost Spark plug/coil issues £60-£200 Vauxhall Astra 1.6/1.8 petrol Idle air control valve £100-£300 Mini Cooper N14 1.6 High-pressure fuel pump £400-£900 Mercedes C-Class M271 1.8 Camshaft adjuster £500-£1,500 Audi A4 EA113 2.0 TFSI PCV valve failure £100-£300 What people think vs reality Don't fall for these common misconceptions “It's just a dirty air filter - cheap fix.” Dirty air filters rarely cause rough idle. It's usually ignition or vacuum. “I'll just drive it - it'll clear.” Rough idle won't clear itself. It will get worse and cause misfires. “A fuel system cleaner will fix it.” Sometimes - if it's a minor injector issue. But most cases need proper repairs. “Rough idle means a big engine problem.” Usually not. 80% of rough idle cases are simple fixes (£60-£400). What to do next Three steps to diagnose rough idle Step 1: Check Engine Light - Is the EML on? Is it flashing? (STOP DRIVING if flashing) Step 2: Note The Pattern - Does it improve when driving? Is it worse when warm? Does it stall? Step 3: Professional Diagnostic (£50-£150) - A technician will read fault codes, check live data (fuel trims, MAF), test ignition system, check for vacuum leaks, and perform compression test if required. Rough idle diagnosis costs £50-£150 at UK independent garages. This includes fault code reading and basic inspection. Can rough idle damage my car? Yes - if it's caused by a misfire, unburnt fuel can damage the catalytic converter (£500-£2,500). Is rough idle an MOT failure? Yes if it affects emissions or if the EML is on. Can a fuel system cleaner fix rough idle? Sometimes - if it's a minor injector issue. But most cases need proper repairs.
